episode.outcome: All members sign except Randolph, Mason and Gerry, and the Convention adjourns sine die. While the last members sign, Franklin remarks that the sun painted on the president's chair is a rising sun.
episode.quote: The Constitution being signed by all the members, except Mr. Randolph, Mr. Mason, and Mr. Gerry, who declined giving it the sanction of their names, the Convention dissolved itself by an adjournment sine die .

episode.outcome: The speech text ends with the motion to add the closing formula, which is agreed to. An editor's note then explains why the speech is ascribed to Franklin.
episode.quote: [The motion was then made for adding the laſt formula, viz. Done in Convention, by the unanimous conſent, &c.: which was agreed to, and added accordingly.]

additions.start: He refused to sign, because he thought
additions.end: most consistent with the public good.
additions.why: This is Randolph's stated reason for refusing at his first rising: nine states will fail to ratify, and confusion will follow. F-E8 stops before it, so story.4 reports only the apology and the reservation, not the cause.

additions.end: no scruples against putting his name to it.
additions.why: Williamson proposed a further way to sign: signing only the letter to Congress. This bears directly on the 'several readings of a signature' in analysis.0 and on the alternative in analysis.1. The draft says only 'several members explained why they would sign' and leaves this proposal out.

additions.start: He alluded to Mr. Blount for one.
additions.end: He alluded to Mr. Blount for one.
additions.why: Footnote 2 states that Williamson's 'some members who disliked the Constitution' included Blount. This connects to Blount's statement in story.5.

claims.sentence: 富兰克林讲稿的措辞在两版间是否有出入，本篇不作断言。
claims.scope: Both full texts were read: U2-FRANK in full, and Franklin's speech in U2-ELLIOT

quote.quote: I CONFESS that I do not entirely approve of this conſtitution at preſent

claims.fix: Both versions are in the reading range, and the wording plainly differs. Madison's version reads 'several parts of this Constitution which I do not at present approve' and 'builders of Babel'; the 1793 version reads 'do not entirely approve' and 'builders of Babylon', and lacks '(if approved by Congress and confirmed by the conventions)'. State that differences exist and give examples, rather than declining to judge.

claims.sentence: whether the wording of Franklin's speech differs between the two versions is not asserted.
claims.scope: Both full texts were read: U2-FRANK in full, and Franklin's speech in U2-ELLIOT

quote.quote: like thoſe of the builders of Babylon

claims.fix: Elliot has 'builders of Babel'. Say the versions differ in wording and give one or two examples.

context_issues.problem: Randolph's first statement omits the reason he gave for refusing: he expected ratification to fail and confusion to follow. Readers see only the apology and the reservation, so the refusal looks like a matter of personal conscience alone.

quote.quote: He refused to sign, because he thought the object of the Convention would be frustrated by the alternative which it presented to the people. Nine states will fail to ratify the plan, and confusion must ensue.

context_issues.problem: The draft says only that the papers were left with the president. It omits that the vote was 10 to 1, with Maryland opposed because of its instructions to its deputies, and that the follow-up resolution passed nem. con.
The draft says several members explained why they would sign but skips Williamson's proposal to sign only the accompanying letter. That proposal was another reading of what a signature should mean.

quote.quote: Mr. WILLIAMSON suggested that the signing should be confined to the letter accompanying the Constitution to Congress

review.overall: The draft's main narrative matches the full source and the outcomes are already in the evidence. Two fixes are needed. First, add Randolph's stated reason for refusing to story.4. Second, revise limits.0's refusal to judge whether the two versions of the speech differ, since both full texts were read and the wording visibly differs.
